title: Ansel and the Vow
premise: Marine biologist Rosalind Nystrom joins a coastal town's anonymous pen-pal program to distract herself from a failed engagement, only to be matched — through a clerical error neither can undo without exposing their letters — with Ansel Vow, the estate lawyer liquidating her late grandmother's beloved sea-turtle sanctuary. As their letters deepen into intimacy, Rosalind discovers Ansel's firm engineered the fraudulent will that gutted the sanctuary, and Ansel must choose between the inheritance that built his career and the woman whose trust he's been winning under a false name. When the true will surfaces in his firm's archives, he burns his professional future to expose the forgery, and Rosalind must forgive him — and herself — before the sanctuary's final auction date. They end not as pen pals but as co-directors of a restored sanctuary, having learned that justice sometimes requires breaking the rules, and love requires telling the truth first.
about_author: Hazel Dravenmoor is a former tide-pool docent who writes love stories set where the land gives way to salt water. She lives on a windswept peninsula with an aging dog named Buoy and a stubborn belief that letters can save people.

chapters.title: Counting Turtles
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Reeling from a broken engagement, she returns to Gullwing Cove to catalog her grandmother's turtle sanctuary ahead of its contested probate. She signs up for the town's anonymous pen-pal program as a distraction. Emotional beat: guarded grief disguised as competence.

chapters.title: The Man with the Ledger
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. He arrives to execute the estate sale, carrying guilt over a case he suspects was mishandled by his firm. He too joins the pen-pal program at his sister's urging. Emotional beat: polished professionalism cracking over private doubt.

chapters.title: Mismatched Ink
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The program's volunteer coordinator misfiles two cards, pairing the enemies instead of strangers. Their first letters are barbed and formal — each unknowingly describing the other as 'the worst person in this town.' Emotional beat: reluctant fascination.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Letters soften; her correspondent asks questions no one else does. Meanwhile she finds irregularities in the estate documents and confronts Ansel in person, sharpening their daytime hostility even as nighttime letters warm. Emotional beat: dramatic irony tightening.

chapters.title: The Forgery Clause
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Digging into firm archives, he confirms his mentor forged the grandmother's will to benefit a developer client. He realizes his pen pal's descriptions match Rosalind exactly — and panics. Emotional beat: complicity curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Low Tide, High Stakes
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A storm strands them together at the sanctuary hatchery; almost-tender moments collide with her discovery that the auction date moved up. She confesses to her pen pal how much she needs one honest ally. Emotional beat: vulnerability offered to the wrong-named man.

chapters.title: The Name in the Envelope
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The coordinator discovers the misfiled match and threatens to reveal it. Ansel races to confess first, but arrives to find Rosalind holding his letter, recognizing his handwriting from the legal documents. Emotional beat: betrayal detonating at the worst moment.

chapters.title: Everything the Firm Owns
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Humiliated and disbarred-threatened, he chooses justice anyway: he extracts the original will, records his mentor's confession, and delivers both to Rosalind and the court, knowing it ends his career. Emotional beat: sacrifice as the only apology that counts.

chapters.title: The Auction
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Climax. At the auction, the restored will voids the sale; the developer storms out, the mentor is arrested. Rosalind reads Ansel's final unsent letter aloud to the crowd — then to him. Emotional beat: public forgiveness, private reckoning still owed.

chapters.title: Second Chances, Better Timing
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Weeks later, they reopen the sanctuary as co-directors, writing one last pair of letters — signed this time. Rosalind admits she must forgive herself for hiding behind turtles; Ansel vows honesty over duty. Emotional beat: quiet, earned hope on the shoreline.
